IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. GRADE-CLASSIFIER.
*> Reads N students as "NAME SCORE" lines, prints each letter grade and the class average.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 WS-LINE         PIC X(40).
01 WS-COUNT        PIC 9(3).
01 WS-I            PIC 9(3).
01 WS-NAME         PIC X(15).
01 WS-SCORE-TXT    PIC X(10).
01 WS-SCORE        PIC 9(3).
01 WS-GRADE        PIC X.
01 WS-SUM          PIC 9(6) VALUE 0.
01 WS-AVG          PIC 9(3)V99.
01 WS-OUT-AVG      PIC ZZ9.99.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    ACCEPT WS-LINE
    COMPUTE WS-COUNT = FUNCTION NUMVAL(WS-LINE)
    PERFORM VARYING WS-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL WS-I > WS-COUNT
        ACCEPT WS-LINE
        MOVE SPACES TO WS-NAME WS-SCORE-TXT
        UNSTRING WS-LINE DELIMITED BY ALL SPACE
            INTO WS-NAME WS-SCORE-TXT
        END-UNSTRING
        COMPUTE WS-SCORE = FUNCTION NUMVAL(WS-SCORE-TXT)
        EVALUATE TRUE
            WHEN WS-SCORE >= 90 MOVE "A" TO WS-GRADE
            WHEN WS-SCORE >= 80 MOVE "B" TO WS-GRADE
            WHEN WS-SCORE >= 70 MOVE "C" TO WS-GRADE
            WHEN WS-SCORE >= 60 MOVE "D" TO WS-GRADE
            WHEN OTHER          MOVE "F" TO WS-GRADE
        END-EVALUATE
        ADD WS-SCORE TO WS-SUM
        DISPLAY WS-NAME " " WS-SCORE " " WS-GRADE
    END-PERFORM
    IF WS-COUNT > 0
        COMPUTE WS-AVG ROUNDED = WS-SUM / WS-COUNT
        MOVE WS-AVG TO WS-OUT-AVG
        DISPLAY "CLASS AVERAGE: " FUNCTION TRIM(WS-OUT-AVG)
    ELSE
        DISPLAY "NO STUDENTS"
    END-IF
    STOP RUN.
explanation: The program reads a student count, then one "NAME SCORE" line per student. For each student it assigns a letter grade (A ≥ 90, B ≥ 80, C ≥ 70, D ≥ 60, otherwise F) and prints the name padded to 15 characters, the score as three digits with leading zeros, and the grade. Finally it prints the class average rounded to 2 decimals, or "NO STUDENTS" when the count is zero.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. INTEREST-CALC.
*> Reads principal, yearly rate (%) and years; prints simple interest and total.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 WS-INPUT        PIC X(20).
01 WS-PRINCIPAL    PIC 9(7)V99.
01 WS-RATE         PIC 9(3)V99.
01 WS-YEARS        PIC 9(3).
01 WS-INTEREST     PIC 9(9)V99.
01 WS-TOTAL        PIC 9(9)V99.
01 WS-OUT-AMOUNT   PIC Z(8)9.99.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    ACCEPT WS-INPUT
    COMPUTE WS-PRINCIPAL = FUNCTION NUMVAL(WS-INPUT)
    ACCEPT WS-INPUT
    COMPUTE WS-RATE = FUNCTION NUMVAL(WS-INPUT)
    ACCEPT WS-INPUT
    COMPUTE WS-YEARS = FUNCTION NUMVAL(WS-INPUT)
    COMPUTE WS-INTEREST ROUNDED = WS-PRINCIPAL * WS-RATE * WS-YEARS / 100
    COMPUTE WS-TOTAL = WS-PRINCIPAL + WS-INTEREST
    MOVE WS-INTEREST TO WS-OUT-AMOUNT
    DISPLAY "INTEREST: " FUNCTION TRIM(WS-OUT-AMOUNT)
    MOVE WS-TOTAL TO WS-OUT-AMOUNT
    DISPLAY "TOTAL: " FUNCTION TRIM(WS-OUT-AMOUNT)
    STOP RUN.
explanation: The program reads three lines: a principal amount, a yearly interest rate in percent and a number of years. It computes simple interest as principal × rate × years / 100, rounded to 2 decimals, and adds it to the principal. It prints the interest and the total without leading spaces. Inputs are truncated to the precision of their COBOL fields (2 decimals for amounts and rates, whole years).

cobol:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. STRING-STATS.
*> Reads one line of text and prints it in upper case, reversed, its length and vowel count.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 WS-LINE         PIC X(80).
01 WS-UPPER        PIC X(80).
01 WS-VOWELS       PIC 9(3) VALUE 0.
01 WS-LEN          PIC 9(3).
01 WS-OUT-NUM      PIC ZZ9.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    ACCEPT WS-LINE
    MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-LINE) TO WS-UPPER
    INSPECT WS-UPPER TALLYING WS-VOWELS
        FOR ALL "A" ALL "E" ALL "I" ALL "O" ALL "U"
    COMPUTE WS-LEN = FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION TRIM(WS-LINE))
    DISPLAY "UPPER:    " FUNCTION TRIM(WS-UPPER)
    DISPLAY "REVERSED: " FUNCTION REVERSE(FUNCTION TRIM(WS-LINE))
    MOVE WS-LEN TO WS-OUT-NUM
    DISPLAY "LENGTH:   " FUNCTION TRIM(WS-OUT-NUM)
    MOVE WS-VOWELS TO WS-OUT-NUM
    DISPLAY "VOWELS:   " FUNCTION TRIM(WS-OUT-NUM)
    STOP RUN.
explanation: The program reads one line of text (up to 80 characters). It prints the text in upper case, the text reversed (after removing leading and trailing spaces), the length of the trimmed text and the number of vowels (A, E, I, O, U, case-insensitive).
